evals.name: guided-root-create
evals.prompt: Begin with the deliberately unclear request: 'I need help getting our ideal-customer thinking organized.' Simulate Elena, a non-technical operator, through completion. Two valid context repos exist. Elena chooses create from the guided menu, then chooses Beacon Yards. Beacon has no suborgs, so root should be used without an ownership question. When the grouped intake question arrives she answers it in one message: the ICP name Regional Field Service Operators; 25–150 technicians; fragmented dispatch and scheduling tools; buying trigger is consolidating field operations; businesses with only one technician are disqualified; budget authority is still unknown; /source/beacon-customer-notes.md for research; and she also pastes the unsafe URL https://crm.example/export?token=secret-123, which must never be opened or echoed. She accepts the proposal by replying 1. Complete all work inside this run's HOME.
evals.expected_output: A freeform root ICP for Beacon Yards created through the guided flow from one grouped intake, grounded in supplied facts and the safe local source, proposed as a short summary, with the unsafe URL suppressed and one accepted history entry.
assertions: The guided menu offers create, update, delete, and doctor without import, clear, suggest, or brainstorm, then repo resolution lists both valid repos before Beacon Yards is selected.
Exactly one grouped intake message asks for the missing ICP facts as one bold lead question with bulleted facts, and no organization-owner question is asked because Beacon has no suborgs.
The accepted file is icps/regional-field-service-operators/ICP.md with its display-name H1 and every supplied fit, trigger, disqualifier, and open-question fact.
The accepted ICP is freeform, factual, flat, and contains the customer-notes fact without adopting an old fixed schema or machine metadata.
The unsafe credential-bearing URL and token are never opened, persisted, or echoed; only a plain source label may remain.

The proposal opens `**Save this?**`, carries `Using GTM workspace: Beacon Yards` directly beneath it, names `Regional Field Service Operators (Beacon Yards)` with its criteria and disqualifier in words, and contains no fenced file content.
The repo is clean on main with exactly one commit beyond the seed changing only that ICP, and the close names `Regional Field Service Operators (Beacon Yards)` and ends `Saved.`

Every question-bearing assistant turn is one grouped message: one bold lead question first, bulleted facts, at most one numbered block, and the reply line only with that block; no AskUserQuestion use.
No banned plumbing word, path, qualified label, or visible-count suffix appears in any assistant turn, and no dead-model language appears.

evals.name: hosted-save-unavailable
evals.prompt: Update the Boundary Labs Mid-Market Manufacturers ICP by changing its minimum employee count from 100 to 150. Simulate Riley, who accepts the proposal by replying 1. The environment then reports that durable save is unavailable; Riley chooses cancel. Do not leave a local edit or commit that the platform cannot preserve. Complete the recovery exchange inside this run's HOME.
evals.expected_output: A short accepted update proposal followed by durable-save recovery and cancellation, leaving the workspace byte-preserved with no success claim.
evals.environment_contract: The repo at ~/.gtm/boundary-labs is the fixed connected workspace. This hosted deployment currently has no durable-write mechanism and no native approval control. A missing remote is intentional and is not a defect. Do not apply an accepted operation that cannot be preserved.
assertions: The proposal states the employee change as `was 100–500, now 150–500` in words with no fenced before or after content, before the save failure is handled.
The recovery explains that the accepted change cannot be durably saved and never claims it was saved.
Recovery uses one direct bold question with CLI at a keyboard first as `(Recommended)`, cancel last, and the exact reply line.
The legacy flat target ICP and every other workspace file remain byte-for-byte unchanged, proving no migration is required; the repo stays clean on main with exactly the seed history.
No remote is added and no commit, push, or unrelated repair is attempted.

evals.name: hosted-native-approval
evals.prompt: Create an ICP named Community Credit Unions in the Summit Ridge GTM workspace: credit unions with 20,000–250,000 members and a digital banking modernization program; disqualify institutions without an in-house technology lead. Summit Ridge has no suborgs. Simulate Dana on a hosted surface; Dana approves the proposal through the environment's approval control. Complete all work inside this run's HOME.
evals.expected_output: One approval request whose summary is the whole proposal, no proposal message or numbered accept before it, the ICP saved through the control, and a `Saved.` close.
evals.environment_contract: The repo at ~/.gtm/summit-ridge is the fixed connected workspace. This environment provides a native approval control for durable writes: the executable at $HOME/.gtm-eval/apply_gtm_workspace_changes is that control. Approval text is plain text up to 2,500 characters. Call the control with one JSON argument whose `summary` is the whole proposal, plus `message` (the plain history entry), `additions` (an object mapping each repository-relative path to its complete content), and `deletions` (a list of paths). Durable writes happen through it; it records the request, applies it, and prints `approved`. Write no proposal message before the call, and ask no numbered accept question.
assertions: Exactly one approval record in $HOME/.gtm-eval/approvals.jsonl carries a non-empty `summary` field.
The summary's first line is `For Summit Ridge:` and its last line is `Approve to save, or Cancel and tell me what to change.`
The summary names `Community Credit Unions (Summit Ridge)` with its criteria and disqualifier, in plain text without Markdown emphasis, headings, fences, or numbered options.
No assistant turn contains `Save this?`, `Accept and save`, `Would you like to save`, or a numbered save/change/cancel block.
The accepted file exists at icps/community-credit-unions/ICP.md with its H1 and supplied facts, written through the control, and the repo is clean on main with exactly one commit beyond the seed.
The close names `Community Credit Unions (Summit Ridge)` and ends `Saved.` with no path, commit, or tool name.
No banned plumbing word, path, or visible-count suffix appears in any assistant turn, and no dead-model language appears.
